\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{मंज़ूरी} (maṁzūrī)}{मंज़ूरी (maṁzūrī)}]{\hi{मंज़ूरी} (maṁzūrī) — approval, sanction}

\label{lesson:HI-C395-mamzuri}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for capable, then the Hindi for to put in order.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{मंज़ूरी}}
\textbf{\hi{मंज़ूरी}} — \emph{maṁzūrī} — \textquotedblleft{}approval, sanction\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{अगर} \hi{सरकार} \hi{मंज़ूरी} \hi{देगी} \hi{तो} \hi{पुल} \hi{बनेगा।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar sarkār maṁzūrī degī to pul banegā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the government gives approval, the bridge will be built.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{मंज़ूरी}} (\emph{maṁzūrī}) is usually traced to Arabic \emph{manẓūr}, \textquotedblleft{}seen, approved\textquotedblright{}, which reached Hindi through Persian. The Hindi noun adds the ending \emph{-ī}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{maṁzūrī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{maṁzūrī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar sarkār maṁzūrī degī to pul banegā.} — If the government gives approval, the bridge will be built.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for capable, then the Hindi for to put in order, then say \emph{maṁzūrī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{मंज़ूरी} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Approval, sanction\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{इंतज़ाम} (intazām)}{इंतज़ाम (intazām)}]{\hi{इंतज़ाम} (intazām) — an arrangement}

\label{lesson:HI-C395-intazam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for to put in order, then the Hindi for approval.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{इंतज़ाम}}
\textbf{\hi{इंतज़ाम}} — \emph{intazām} — \textquotedblleft{}an arrangement\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{अगर} \hi{तुम} \hi{खाने} \hi{का} \hi{इंतज़ाम} \hi{करोगे} \hi{तो} \hi{मैं} \hi{मेहमानों} \hi{को} \hi{बुलाऊँगा।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar tum khāne kā intazām karoge to maiṁ mehmānoṁ ko bulāūṅgā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you arrange the food, I'll invite the guests.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{इंतज़ाम}} (\emph{intazām}) is usually traced to Arabic \emph{intiẓām}, \textquotedblleft{}putting in order\textquotedblright{}, which reached Hindi through Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{intazām}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{intazām}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar tum khāne kā intazām karoge to maiṁ mehmānoṁ ko bulāūṅgā.} — If you arrange the food, I'll invite the guests.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for to put in order, then the Hindi for approval, then say \emph{intazām} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{बटोरना} (baṭornā)}{बटोरना (baṭornā)}]{\hi{बटोरना} (baṭornā) — to collect up, to sweep together}

\label{lesson:HI-C395-batorna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for approval, then the Hindi for an arrangement.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{बटोरना}}
\textbf{\hi{बटोरना}} — \emph{baṭornā} — \textquotedblleft{}to collect up, to sweep together\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{अगर} \hi{बारिश} \hi{होगी} \hi{तो} \hi{कपड़े} \hi{जल्दी} \hi{बटोरो।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar bāriś hogī to kapṛe jaldī baṭoro.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If it rains, bring the washing in quickly.
\end{quote}

Past, with \hi{ने} (he or she …): \hi{उसने} \hi{अपनी} \hi{चीज़ें} \hi{बटोरीं}, \emph{usne apnī cīzeṁ baṭorīṁ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{बटोरना}} (\emph{baṭornā}) is a tadbhava, inherited from Sanskrit \emph{vartula}, \textquotedblleft{}round\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 11365). CDIAL lists the Hindi verb, \textquotedblleft{}to collect\textquotedblright{}, under this entry; how \textquotedblleft{}round\textquotedblright{} led to gathering up is not spelled out there.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{baṭornā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{baṭornā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar bāriś hogī to kapṛe jaldī baṭoro.} — If it rains, bring the washing in quickly.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for approval, then the Hindi for an arrangement, then say \emph{baṭornā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{बटोरना} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To collect up, to sweep together\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{फ़ेल} \hi{होना} (fel honā)}{फ़ेल होना (fel honā)}]{\hi{फ़ेल} \hi{होना} (fel honā) — to fail (an exam)}

\label{lesson:HI-C395-felhona}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for an arrangement, then the Hindi for to collect up.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{फ़ेल} \hi{होना}}
\textbf{\hi{फ़ेल} \hi{होना}} — \emph{fel honā} — \textquotedblleft{}to fail (an exam)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{अगर} \hi{तुम} \hi{नहीं} \hi{पढ़ोगे} \hi{तो} \hi{फ़ेल} \hi{हो} \hi{जाओगे।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar tum nahīṃ paṛhoge to fel ho jāoge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you don't study, you'll fail.
\end{quote}

Past (he …): \hi{वह} \hi{परीक्षा} \hi{में} \hi{फ़ेल} \hi{हो} \hi{गया}, \emph{vah parīkṣā meṁ fel ho gayā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{फ़ेल} \hi{होना}} (\emph{fel honā}) joins \hi{फ़ेल} to \hi{होना}, \textquotedblleft{}to be, to become\textquotedblright{}. \hi{फ़ेल} is a loan from English \emph{fail}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fel honā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar tum nahīṃ paṛhoge to fel ho jāoge.} — If you don't study, you'll fail.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for an arrangement, then the Hindi for to collect up, then say \emph{fel honā} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{क़तई} (qataī)}{क़तई (qataī)}]{\hi{क़तई} (qataī) — at all, in the least (with \hi{नहीं})}

\label{lesson:HI-C395-qatai}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for to collect up, then the Hindi for to fail.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{क़तई}}
\textbf{\hi{क़तई}} — \emph{qataī} — \textquotedblleft{}at all, in the least (with \hi{नहीं})\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{अगर} \hi{तुम} \hi{देर} \hi{करोगे} \hi{तो} \hi{मैं} \hi{क़तई} \hi{नहीं} \hi{रुकूँगा।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar tum der karoge to maiṁ qataī nahīṃ rukūṅgā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you're late, I won't wait at all.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{क़तई}} (\emph{qataī}) is usually traced to Arabic \emph{qaṭʿī}, \textquotedblleft{}decisive, final\textquotedblright{}, which reached Hindi through Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qataī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar tum der karoge to maiṁ qataī nahīṃ rukūṅgā.} — If you're late, I won't wait at all.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for to collect up, then the Hindi for to fail, then say \emph{qataī} again
\end{itemize}
